claims.claim: The workflow accepts exactly one environment-bound dispatch_id alongside TASK id and Executor, validates bounded opaque syntax, and preserves the A1 runner, permission, credential, checkout, synchronization, and verification boundaries.
First-seen dispatches atomically persist hashed repository-local .git/aios journal state and pre-invocation RUN namespace before delegating once to the existing PRIMARY path.
Terminal dispatch re-delivery never reinvokes PRIMARY and preserves the recorded dispatch/RUN attribution and original success or nonzero failure outcome.

Nonterminal dispatches observationally reconcile uniquely attributable RUN, RESULT, FAILURE, active-lock, incomplete, zero-candidate, and ambiguous-candidate states without retry, recovery, cleanup, or synthetic artifacts.
Direct aios run and existing Operator/Runtime ownership remain unchanged; aios wakeup is only an outer identity and reconciliation boundary.
README documents stable dispatch identity, replay and restart semantics, operational-only state, and authority separation; the roadmap records A2 via TASK-068 while later gates remain separate.
